summary:
The "No Visas for Anti-Semitic Students Act" directs the Secretary of State to revoke or deny F or M nonimmigrant visas to aliens engaging in antisemitic conduct that poses adverse foreign policy consequences. 

Section 2 establishes a mandatory visa revocation or denial mechanism. The Secretary of State shall revoke or deny a visa under section 101(a)(15)(F) or (M) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)) to any alien who, on or after the date of enactment, engages in "prohibited antisemitic conduct" and is determined by the Secretary, pursuant to section 237(a)(4)(C)(i) of the INA (8 U.S.C. 1227(a)(4)(C)(i)), to pose potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences for the United States through such conduct. The section defines "antisemitism" by reference to the May 26, 2016, International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) definition adopted by the Department of State, including its contemporary examples. "Prohibited antisemitic conduct" is defined as engaging in a physical act of violence, vandalism, or harassment targeting a Jewish individual, their property, a community institution, or religious facility, with intent to intimidate or harm based on Jewish identity or affiliation; or providing material support (including funding, organizing, or inciting) to a person knowing the person intended to use such support to engage in such an act.

Section 3 amends section 214 of the INA (8 U.S.C. 1184) by adding a new subsection (s). Subsection (s)(1) provides that an alien may not be granted or maintain nonimmigrant status under INA section 101(a)(15)(F) or (M) if the alien engages in prohibited antisemitic conduct and the Secretary of State determines, pursuant to INA section 237(a)(4)(C)(i), that such conduct would have potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences. Subsection (s)(2) imposes a mandatory duty on the Secretary to revoke the visa of an alien granted F or M nonimmigrant status if the Secretary determines the alien engaged in prohibited antisemitic conduct posing potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences. Subsection (s)(3) incorporates the same definitions of "antisemitism" and "prohibited antisemitic conduct" as provided in section 2. The Act does not include specific appropriations; it establishes new authorities and mandates for the executive branch. The operative trigger for visa denial or revocation under section 2 applies to conduct occurring on or after the date of enactment.
